title: A Genetic Algorithm to Model Solar Radio Active Regions From 3D Magnetic Field Extrapolations
question: Determine the plasma temperature and electron density height profiles in the solar atmosphere of active region NOAA 12470 to reproduce observed radio brightness temperature maps at 17, 100, and 230 GHz.

what.value: Quiet Sun brightness temperatures at 230 GHz (6210 ± 110 K) and 100 GHz (7110 ± 90 K)

evidence.loc: Radio maps
evidence.quote: While the quiet Sun brightness temperature ( $T_\mathrm{b,QS}$) at 230 GHz is $6210\pm110$ K (cite: Selhorst2019), the AR 12470 brightness temperature ($T_\mathrm{b}$) varies from 5800 to 6600 K

evidence.loc: Radio maps
evidence.quote: At 100 GHz, $T_{qS}=7110\pm90$ K (cite: Selhorst2019) and AR 12470 showed $T_\mathrm{b}$ varying from 7200 to 7650 K where $|\vec{B}|>1500$ G.

what.value: Initial 1D quiet Sun atmospheric seed model (SSC)

evidence.loc: Genetic Algorithm Features
evidence.quote: The atmospheric model developed by (cite: Selhorst2005b) is used as the seed in the genetic algorithm, that changes the seed model to find the best fit for the observational measurements.

what.value: Minimum magnetic field intensity of 1500 G to form a sunspot

evidence.loc: Results
evidence.quote: The $|\vec{B}|$ limits used to classify each pixel are based on studies by (cite: Livingston2012), who derived a minimum necessary value of 1500 G for sunspot formation.

recipe.goal: Prepare, deproject, and co-align magnetogram and radio maps
recipe.method: Rotate AR in HMI LOS magnetogram to solar disk center, remove solar spherical curvature, correct magnetic field intensities for projection effects, longitudinally rotate radio maps to match magnetogram time, resize radio maps to match magnetogram grid (4096x4096), and crop/resize selected active region area from 1024x1024 to 256x256 pixels (~2"/pixel).
key_parameters: Longitudinal rotation: -0.01 deg (230 GHz), -2.85 deg (100 GHz), 7.31 deg (17 GHz)
assumptions: |B| is 7.5% greater than observed B_z due to heliographic position (17.40°N, 17.68°E)

recipe.goal: Extrapolate 3D coronal and chromospheric magnetic field from photospheric magnetogram
recipe.method: Perform linear force-free field (LFF) extrapolation above the photosphere starting from the line-of-sight magnetic field component to generate 3D cubes of Bx, By, Bz and field line positions, and interpolate voxel height resolution to 50 km.
key_parameters: Vertical voxel height resolution h_z = 50 km
assumptions: Linear force-free field approximation (current density parallel to magnetic field at any point in space)

recipe.goal: Classify pixels by photospheric magnetic field strength
recipe.method: Classify each pixel in the magnetogram into four classes based on photospheric magnetic field intensity |B|_0: umbra, penumbra, plage, and quiet Sun.
key_parameters: Umbra: |B| >= 1500 G (~200 pixels); Penumbra: 1000 <= |B_0| < 1500 G (~230 pixels); Plages: 200 <= |B_0| < 1000 G (~27200 pixels); Quiet Sun: |B| <= 200 G (~38000 pixels)
assumptions: Pixels with |B| <= 200 G have quiet Sun brightness temperature T_B = T_qS

recipe.goal: Fit 1D atmospheric temperature and density profiles per pixel via genetic algorithm and radiative transfer
recipe.method: Run Pikaia genetic algorithm independently for each vertical column (pixel) to modify the seed SSC quiet Sun model via 5 free parameters, compute thermal bremsstrahlung and gyroresonance absorption coefficients and 1D radiative transfer to obtain T_b at 17, 100, and 230 GHz, minimize chi-squared against observations, and average best-fit profiles per class.
key_parameters: 5 free parameters: chromospheric temperature gradient, chromospheric electron density gradient, coronal temperature factor N_T, coronal electron density factor N_n_e, and TR position shift Delta h

GA settings: full-generation replacement, 10 generations, 100 children per generation, crossover probability = 0.85, variable mutation mode, initial mutation rate = 0.005, mutation rate range = 0.0005 to 0.25
Gyroresonance harmonics s <= 5 with 10% uncertainty in |B| (3rd harmonic at 2000±200 G, 4th at 1500±150 G, 5th at 1200±120 G)
assumptions: Effective ion charge Z = 1.178, only electron-proton collisions considered, densities grouped as (n_e * n_i)^(1/2), plasma fully ionized above 1000 km in SSC model

recipe.goal: Convolve synthetic radio maps with instrumental beams and compare with observations
recipe.method: Convolve the 2" resolution GA model brightness temperature maps with 2D Gaussian beams matching observational resolutions (25" at 230 GHz, 58" at 100 GHz, 10" at 17 GHz) and compare average brightness temperatures across umbra, penumbra, plages, and polarized/non-polarized regions.
key_parameters: 2D Gaussian beam FWHM: 25" (230 GHz), 58" (100 GHz), 10" (17 GHz)

evidence.loc: Abstract
evidence.quote: for umbrae the TR is located at $1080\pm20$ km above the solar surface;

evidence.loc: Results

Exact functional mathematical equations for how the five GA free parameters modify the SSC temperature and density height profiles
Details of the initial seed parameters used for each distinct AR class (umbrae, penumbrae, plages) to speed up the GA

Exact formulation of the chi-squared objective function (including observational uncertainty weights for the three frequencies and whether beam convolution is applied before or after pixel-by-pixel chi-squared evaluation)
Which magneto-ionic mode (o-mode, x-mode, or average of both) was used in the radiative transfer integration to compare with total intensity maps
missing_for_reproduction: Exact mathematical equations defining how the 5 free parameters (chromospheric gradients, coronal multipliers, and TR shift) modify the seed SSC height profile
Minimum and maximum parameter search bounds supplied to Pikaia for each of the 5 free parameters and for each of the 3 AR region classes
Custom IDL code for the radiative transfer, Pikaia wrapper, and LFF extrapolation (unless using GX Simulator in SolarSoft)
Exact bounding box coordinates used to crop the 1024x1024 active region area from the full-disk 4096x4096 HMI magnetogram
score_reason: All observational data (ALMA SV, SDO/HMI, NoRH) are public and exact timestamps, rotation angles, grid dimensions, GA hyperparameters, radiative transfer equations, and final tabulated model profiles are provided; however, the exact mathematical parameterization of the 5 GA modifications to the SSC profile and their prior search ranges are not explicitly written out.
rediscovery_reason: All input datasets (ALMA SV 2011.0.00020.SV, SDO/HMI, NoRH) are public, the physical equations and GA settings are well specified, and the paper provides clear numeric answer keys (TR heights and region-averaged brightness temperatures).
